Subject: Control plane / data plane ownership and routing validation for on-prem VPC

Alex / team —

Thanks again for the session yesterday. I promised to consolidate the outstanding ownership and routing questions so we can sign off on the network demarc for the private deployment. Attached is a concise reference (vpc-control-data-ownership-v1.pdf) and an updated topology snapshot (attachment-diagram-v2.png). Main asks below: 

- Confirm which ACME subnets will be used for the control plane management network vs. data plane tenant traffic (we marked them as 10.100.0.0/22 and 10.200.0.0/20 in the diagram).
- Egress policy: is colo egress via the provider NAT (COL0-NAT-1) acceptable for tenant telemetry, or must outbound flow from runtime nodes be hairpinned through ACME perimeter firewall? If the latter, we need expected latency headroom.
- Route target ownership: Redwood will own 100.64.10.0/24 (service sidecars) and ACME will advertise the on-prem tenant prefixes. Confirm BGP ASNs and next-hop reachability so we can generate the BGP neighbors config.
- Evidence for compliance: the security team requested an export of allowed outbound ports for runtime metrics/obs; I attached a starter CSV (egress-allowed-ports.csv) — please augment with any blocked ports.

Can we aim to close these by EOW? If helpful, I can stand up a 30-minute call with ACME neteng + Kimberly to walk the diagram and capture final edits.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ACME Network Engineering <neteng@acme-corp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-29T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control plane / data plane ownership and routing validation for on-prem VPC

Jordan —

Thanks for pulling this together. Quick answers inline: 

- Subnets: we can commit to 10.100.0.0/22 (control plane management) and 10.200.0.0/20 (tenant data). We'll send the official CIDR assignment sheet — neteng will attach to this thread by EOD.
- Egress policy: colo provider prefers NAT for general outbound. However, for compliance-sensitive telemetry (our SOC process) we require a hairpin through the perimeter firewall for flows marked as controlled (port 443 to redwood-endpoints we specify). I'll attach the mandatory egress ACLs separately. That hairpin will add ~4–8ms baseline latency; I flagged this with our infra lead.
- BGP: ACME will advertise tenant prefixes. Our ASNs: AS64521 for ACME edge; we can peer with the ASN you provide. Next hop will be the colo fabric gateway 203.0.113.5.

Attaching: acme-egress-acls.pdf and acme-subnet-assignment.xlsx. Let me know if you want a quick screen-share — we can do 11am PT tomorrow.

—Alex
Network Lead, Acme Corp
alex.rivera@acme-corp.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-29T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control plane / data plane ownership and routing validation for on-prem VPC

Alex / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side before we lock configs: 

1) BGP ASN: Redwood will present AS65310 for the service-side neighbors. We will originate 100.64.10.0/24 (sidecar-control) and 100.64.11.0/24 (kv-cache-relay), both with MED set to prefer local fabric for intra-colo traffic.

2) Egress hairpin: we can support the hairpin pattern but need the firewall ACLs as explicit rules (destination FQDNs and ports). Our runtime health checks to Redwood endpoints use TLS on 443 and mTLS on 8443; please ensure those are allowed. If ACME requires proxying through their perimeter, we need the outbound proxy details (FQDN/IP and TLS intercept behavior) so our metrics exporter can be configured.

3) Observability: Neha and I will generate a short checklist for the SOC evidence request once we have the final egress ACLs and BGP neighbor IPs. I'll draft the checklist and post to the Drive folder you linked.

Action items:
- ACME: attach subnet assignment and egress ACLs (Alex) — due 2026-12-29 EOD (Alex said EOD).
- Jordan / Kimberly: produce final BGP neighbor template and runbook (Jordan to draft; Kimberly to review) — target 2026-12-30.
- Neha: prepare SOC evidence checklist skeleton — target 2026-12-30.

Kimberly Park
Principal Cloud Network Engineer | Redwood Inference

- The perimeter team confirmed they can allow TLS outbound to your endpoints but will terminate TLS for inspection; they require a short list of hostnames. Jordan, can you provide the hostnames for healthchecks/metrics/call-home?
- We will provision BGP neighbors tomorrow morning (203.0.113.5 <-> 198.51.100.11). AS64521 <-> AS65310.

Thanks — Alex
